item.title: Yellow lines needed, 13th August
item.description:
When the road is busy with people parking to go to the park, which is most weekends and often throughout the summer holidays, people park on this bend and on the straight side of the road opposite. This results in a narrowing of the space for cars driving through, so only one car can fit, at the same time as absolutely no view around the bend. Many times I have cautiously driven up to the bend and someone has been speeding down Thicket Road to cross over to the one way part. I have also seen traffic build up because of this and many near accidents. It is a terrible accident waiting to happen and if there were just yellow lines on both sides of the road, especially on the bend, this could be easily avoided. Please consider doing this before it is too late.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 4, Anerley Park Road, Crystal Palace, Greater London

item.title: Fire risk: Rubbish is permanently being dumped outside flat building, 13th August
item.description:
There is persistent fly-tipping taking place in the area immediately outside our residential building. People are accessing the site from the main street and via the adjacent church area and are throwing rubbish over/through the boundary into this space. As shown in the attached photos, a significant amount of waste, discarded furniture, building materials and other rubbish has accumulated. The area is becoming increasingly hazardous and is directly adjacent to residential properties. This presents a serious potential fire hazard, given the quantity of combustible waste being stored in a confined area immediately next to the buildings. It also creates a risk to residents and encourages further fly-tipping. I would ask that the council: • Clear all of the illegally dumped waste and debris from the site. • Properly secure and board/fence off the access points from the main street and the adjacent church area so that people can no longer enter or throw rubbish into the site. • Ensure that any existing damaged or inadequate barriers are properly repaired or replaced, rather than simply removing the current rubbish. • Consider measures such as secure fencing/gates or other appropriate preventative measures to stop the fly-tipping from recurring. • Assess the site for any fire or other health and safety risks arising from the accumulated waste. This is not an isolated item of litter but an ongoing fly-tipping problem caused by people being able to access the area. Simply removing the existing rubbish without securing the area is likely to result in the problem recurring. I would appreciate this being treated as a priority due to the proximity of the accumulated combustible waste to residential buildings and the potential fire risk.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Warwick Court, Greater London
